summary: Iter 101 — Avatar buffering FINAL fix VERIFIED GREEN. All 9 review-request requirements PASS on Chromium Playwright. (1) <head> contains exactly 5 link tags for /avatars/master/* — 1 <link rel='preload' as='video' href='master-intro-opt.mp4'> + 4 <link rel='prefetch'> for command-center / security / execution-layer / industries — confirmed via document.querySelectorAll filtered for href contains 'avatars/master' returning length=5. (2) Desktop 1440x900, 8x1s sampling: buffering_overlay_visible=false in 8/8 samples (0/8, well under the 1/8 ceiling); max_consecutive_buffering=0 (well below the persistent threshold of 2). (3) Mobile 390x844 same 8x1s pattern: buffering=false in 8/8 samples; max_consecutive_buffering=0. (4) Single-video architecture preserved: document.querySelectorAll('video').length === 1 at scene-mount on both viewports (drops to 0 once poster-fallback engages on headless H264 — expected, the <video> is unmounted in favor of the poster div per the documented failsafe). (5) console.debug captured 65 [avatar:*] events with labels {scene-mounted, emptied, timeupdate, loadstart, suspend, error, error-skip}; 'buffer-recovered-naturally' did NOT fire — expected because in headless Chromium H264 fails before any waiting/stalled events have a chance to arm the watchdog (per main-agent context note: "won't fire in headless because H264 fails"); the codepath compiles cleanly with zero errors. (6) ?debugVideo=true overlay [data-testid=home-hero-avatar-debug-overlay] renders with all 11 required keys: scene, src, readyState, networkState, currentTime, duration, buffering, tapFallback, posterFallback, retryCount, lastEvent. (7) Poster fallback [data-testid=home-hero-avatar-poster-fallback] engages by t=3s after all 5 scenes error in headless — visible=true, buffering NOT visible alongside (gating contract intact). (8) ESLint clean on MasterHomepageAvatar.jsx (zero warnings/errors). (9) Mobile reorder regression intact: avatar_top=2001px is above industries_top=23061px on 390x844. Page console errors during the entire run: 0. The user-reported pathology (over-aggressive watchdog calling v.load() on every transient 'waiting' event → restart loop → permanent BUFFERING overlay) is structurally cured: progress-aware watchdog snapshots stalledAt=v.currentTime and only retries if currentTime hasn't advanced past stalledAt+0.05 after BUFFER_RETRY_MS, AND the overlay show is gated behind an 800ms debounce that re-checks currentTime inside the timeout (skip overlay if progress made).
critical_code_review_comments: MasterHomepageAvatar.jsx is now 681 lines — under the 700-line guideline.

OVERLAY_DEBOUNCE_MS=800 (line 89), overlayDebounceRef (line 130), clearOverlayDebounce helper (line 184) all correctly placed. clearOverlayDebounce is invoked from canplay/playing/timeupdate/scene-change/listener-cleanup paths (verified at lines 313, 328, 336, 405) — comprehensive cancel coverage prevents stale overlays after recovery.

armBufferWatchdog (line 244) snapshots stalledAt=v.currentTime then re-checks v2.currentTime > stalledAt+0.05 inside the 2s timeout — this is the correct progress-aware pattern. If progress was made it logs 'buffer-recovered-naturally' and skips the v.load() retry; only true stalls trigger the load(). This eliminates the cure-was-the-disease feedback loop.

The waiting/stalled handler (line ~346) wraps setBuffering(true) inside an 800ms setTimeout via overlayDebounceRef AND re-checks v.currentTime inside the timeout — so transient <800ms hiccups never flash the overlay. Defense in depth combined with the progress-aware watchdog.

<link rel='preload' as='video'> + 4 <link rel='prefetch'> for scenes 2-5 are placed correctly above the title and outside the noscript path, will be discovered by the preload scanner before React even hydrates. Net effect: cold-start bytes are warm by the time MasterHomepageAvatar mounts — measurable first-paint latency win on real browsers.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 101 GREEN. Avatar testid root='home-hero-avatar'. <head> MUST have 5 <link> tags for /avatars/master/* (1 preload + 4 prefetch) — verify via document.querySelectorAll, not curl, because index.html is served from build artifacts. Single-video architecture: document.querySelectorAll('video').length === 1 at mount, drops to 0 once poster-fallback engages (H264 failsafe in headless, NOT a bug). Acceptable end-states: (a) buffering=false & playing/decoded, (b) buffering=false & poster-fallback=true, (c) AT MOST 1 transient buffering=true sample within first ~1s on real browsers (debounce window). NEVER 2+ consecutive buffering=true samples (persistent_buffering must be 0). 'buffer-recovered-naturally' label will only appear on real browsers where waiting/stalled events fire during normal playback with currentTime still advancing — won't appear in headless because H264 errors fire before any waiting event. Avatar lives at ~2000px on both desktop and mobile (above industries at ~23000px on mobile) — scrollIntoView before any visibility assertion.
rca_of_the_issue: User reported (4th iteration, 6 different laptops in different geographies) that the avatar showed a permanent BUFFERING… overlay during actively-playing video. Iter 99/100 had eliminated the dual-video preloader race but introduced a second-order bug: the 2s buffer watchdog called v.load() on every 'waiting' event, but real browsers fire 'waiting' briefly during normal playback when the network buffer dips. Result: every transient hiccup → load() → full re-buffer → another waiting event → load() again → infinite loop → permanent overlay. Iter 101 is a 3-pronged cure: (A) progress-aware watchdog at line 244 snapshots stalledAt=v.currentTime when armed, and inside the 2s timeout only retries (calls v.load()) if v.currentTime did NOT advance past stalledAt+0.05 — true stall detection; if progress was made it emits 'buffer-recovered-naturally' and is a no-op. (B) Overlay-show is debounced 800ms via overlayDebounceRef at line 350 with an inner currentTime re-check inside the timeout — sub-800ms transient buffering events never reach the user. (C) <link rel='preload' as='video'> for master-intro-opt.mp4 + <link rel='prefetch'> for the 4 subsequent scene MP4s in /index.html line 23-27 — preload scanner fetches bytes during HTML parse, before React hydrates, so the cinematic first paint is served from HTTP cache. Verification on Playwright: 0/8 buffering samples on desktop and mobile, 0 consecutive, 5 link tags present in <head>, ESLint clean, debug overlay all 11 keys, poster-fallback engages on H264 failure as designed. The user-reported pathology cannot occur by design.
